newsitem.title: USA: NHL ICE HOCKEY-COLORADO BEATS DETROIT TO TAKE 1-0 WESTERN CONFERENCE LEAD.
newsitem.headline: NHL ICE HOCKEY-COLORADO BEATS DETROIT TO TAKE 1-0 WESTERN CONFERENCE LEAD.

text.p: Joe Sakic and Mike Ricci scored third-period goals and Patrick Roy stopped 34 shots as the Colorado Avalanche escaped with a 2-1 victory over the Detroit Red Wings in the opener of the best-of-seven Western Conference finals on Thursday.
Colorado remained perfect at home in the postseason, despite being outshot, 35-19, and being held without a power-play goal for the first time in nine games.
Sakic lifted the Avalanche into a 1-1 tie at 1:40 of the third period, 27 seconds after Brendan Shanahan's goal broke a scoreless tie.

Eric Lacroix drew two defenders in the left corner, but managed to centre the puck while he was being taken down. Sakic took the pass at the left faceoff circle and wristed a shot through goaltender Mike Vernon's pads for his fifth playoff goal.

Sakic also figured in Colorado's go-ahead goal at 6:13. He carried into the Detroit zone and sent the puck to Claude Lemieux at the right faceoff circle. Lemieux slid a pass in front to Mike Ricci, who was left alone down the slot and deflected the puck into the open half of the net for his second postseason goal and first in 11 games.
The rest was up to Roy, the winningest goalie in playoff history.
He never saw Bob Rouse's deflection from the slot with just under seven minutes remaining, but got his right skate on it to preserve the lead.
Roy was at his best after Avalanche defenceman Sylvain Lefebvre went off for elbowing with 6:53 to play, coming up with a pair of point-blank stops on Sergei Fedorov in a 25-second span.
Colorado, which is 7-0 at home in the playoffs, hosts Game Two on Saturday.
